description: Acknowledging a message only after processing it, so nothing is lost but a crash before the acknowledgement causes a redelivery.
A consumer for which processing the same message twice has the same effect as processing it once, usually by storing the message id with the side effect in one transaction.
A table of processed message ids, keyed by message id and consumer, written in the same transaction as the business change so duplicates are rejected.
Waiting longer before each new retry, typically doubling the delay (1 s, 2 s, 4 s), so a struggling dependency gets time to recover.
A message that fails every time it is processed, such as invalid data or a bug, and must be moved aside instead of retried forever.
A queue that holds messages a broker or consumer gave up on, for inspection, repair and resubmission.
Saving outgoing messages in an outbox table in the same database transaction as the business data, then publishing them from a background relay.
An Azure Service Bus feature that drops sends repeating a `MessageId` within a time window, which reduces producer duplicates but does not make consumers idempotent.
